characters.name: Dexter
characters.description: A scientificChild Prodigyboy genius who owns a secret lab in his house. Despite his high intelligence, Dexter often finds himself in many conflicts, from his backfired experiments to his ditzy older sister invading his lab and causing trouble. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: He heavily emphasizes the second and third syllables of "laboratory", causing it to sound like "lah-boratory". The Ace: When it comes to science, of course. There was even an episode where one of his teachersclearly has the hots for himbecause of this. Aloof Big Brother:Invertedas he's actually younger than her, but due to being preoccupied with his lab work, he is distant from his immature older sisterDee-Deeand gets mad whenever she invades his lab. Always Someone Better: Proves to be this to Mandark, especially by end of the latter's first appearance. Best shown in "Mandarker" where the two compete in a science fair. Mandark is an inconsolable mess still hung up on his destroyed lab and has to resort to supernatural methods because he can't come up with anything on his own, while Dexter effortlessly impresses the judges with one of his "scribbles" and has moved on from being forced to shut down his lab.

characters.name: Dee Dee
characters.description: Dexter's elder sister, who tends to behave as though she's much younger. She's aditzyDumb BlondeandCloudcuckoolanderwho often finds herself invading her brother's laboratory and messing with his inventions, often to a fatal fault. Accidental Hero:At the end ofEgo Trip, it's her typical stupidity that reverses the effects of the neurotomic protocore that Mandark used to make everyone idiots. The Dexters are irritated by this to no end. Action Girl: She doesn't show it all too often, but when she has to (usually when Dexter is in danger), she can be a certifiedOne-Woman Army, as evidenced by her rescue of him from an alien jail. All Girls Like Ponies: She loves ponies so much, she once asks Dexter to turn her into one. Annoying Younger Sibling: Inverted. She's an AnnoyingOlderSibling to Dexter, constantly breaking his stuff, among other things.

characters.name: Mom
characters.description: '80s Hair: The flashback episode "Glove at First Sight" showed Mom dressed as aValley Girlwith a side ofMaterial Girlwhich included a side ponytail and fluffy bangs. For the big New Years Eve dance, she wears her hair in an asymmetrical bob that looks veryMolly Ringwald-esque. Abusive Parents: Downplayed, as she isn't horribly abusive, but as shown in several episodes, such as "Dee Dee Locks and the Ness Monster", Dexter's mom can be harsh, yelling at and scaring Dexter into doing what she tells him to despite Dexter having reasons to not want to, like not wanting to catch Dee Dee's sickness. Action Mom: Demonstrated in "Mom and Jerry", "World's Greatest Mom" and "A Mom Cartoon". Dexter's mother has shown to be able to fight very well. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Most notably in the episode "Chess Mom", where she embarrasses her son while trying to cheer him on at the chess tournament. Berserk Button:As seen in "Dexter's Rude Removal", the most Mom ever got beyond angry was when the rude clones of Dexter and Deedee not only made a huge mess of her kitchen during a food fight but used profanity as well.Talking back to her, as Dexter learned in the episode "Dexter is Dirty".Germs, period.Also seeing mice in her kitchen.As shown in "A Mom Cartoon" she will deliver aNo-Holds-Barred Beatdownto anyone who gets between her and a blue light special sale at the store that she has her sights set on. That other housewife threw the first kick, but responding with a one two kick combo andrepeatingthat combo several times while the other housewife can't fight back, then beating and stuffing her into the kids' seating area of her own shopping cart while giving her both a black eye and a fat lip screams something else entirely. Especially when she grabs the item afterwards and walks away like nothing happened!

characters.name: Dad
characters.description: '80s Hair: "Glove at First Sight" shows him with a mullet with hair down his neck and bangs that stand out. Abusive Parents: Downplayed, as he isn't horribly abusive, but as shown in several episodes, such as "Better Off Wet", Dexter's dad can be a bully, embarrassing and pulling childish pranks on his family for his own enjoyment. These often include pushing his family in the pool, and very manipulative behavior. He also forces Dexter to literally sleep in the doghouse at one point as a punishment. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Has a tendency to humiliate his kids by accident. Art Evolution: His appearance after the reboot has the biggest redesign of all the characters, with him having a different shade of blonde hair, being a lot skinnier, and has a larger head. Berserk Button: You can threaten him, you can break his car and he'll just brush it off. But don'tevernot-hold a door open for a lady—ESPECIALLY his wife!

characters.name: Mandark
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: Is head-over-heels in love with Dee Dee, who is disgusted by his geekiness. Action Figure Justification: In "Babe Sitter", he angrily tells Dee Dee that his toys are action figures, not dolls. Always Someone Better: He was this to Dexter beforeVillain Decaykicked in. Inverted in "Ego Trip", where, despite their competitiveness,Dexterturns out to be the better one, prompting Mandark to steal Dexter's ideas. Even the Neurotomic Protocore that Mandark uses to brain-drain the entire planet is Dexter's creation, meant to originallyenhancethe world population's intelligence rather than reduce it. Ambiguously Jewish: He's never shown to be religious whatsoever but his last name does imply Russian-Jewish ancestry. Animal Motifs: Mandark is associated with ducks. He has a pet duck named Ducky (who is secretly the supervillain, Quackor the Fowl), and inComic Stripper, he copied the fighting moves of a comic book character named Dangerous Duck, as well as quacking and acting like a duck.

characters.name: Lee Lee and Mee Mee
characters.description: Alphabetical Theme Naming: Their names rhyme with Dee Dee's. Asian Airhead: Lee Lee is Asian, and she and Mee Mee are often depicted as being just as ditzy as Dee Dee. Though "Techno Turtle" shows they're at least marginally smarter than her, since they were able to tell immediately that 'Birdy' was actually a turtle. They also had enough common sense to understand Dee Dee wanting to literally become a horse inDee Dee's Tailwas a ridiculous thing to be upset about. Asian Speekee Engrish: In her first appearance, Lee Lee spoke with a very stunted and stereotypical Asian accent. Every appearance she made afterwards has her speaking normally. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Neither of them is anywhere to be seen in the third and fourth seasons. Color-Coded for Your Convenience: In "That Crazy Robot", Mee Mee wears purple and Lee Lee wears green.

characters.name: Koosalagoopagoop
characters.description: All of the Other Reindeer: It is shown in the episode "Koosalagoopagoop" that everyone else in the Land of Koos dislikes him for some unexplained reason (likely due to his clumsiness), though this changes at the end of the episode. Big Fun: He's a huge and obese creature and really loves to have fun. Blatant Lies: Whether he's downplaying his ability to change size or insisting he's king of Koosland, he's a bit of a chronic liar. The Cameo: He makes a cameo inThe Powerpuff Girlsepisode "Imaginary Fiend", imagined by Bubbles to combat Patches. All of the jokes surrounding himinvolve everyone else's dislike of him. Classy Cane: Briefly carries one when we first see him.

characters.name: T.V. Puppet Pals
characters.description: A pair of slapstick puppet performers who are popular in both Dexter's universe and theJustice Friendsuniverse. Bait-and-Switch: Inthis segment, Mitch asks Clem the question: "to bonk or not to bonk?". Clem responds with "not", leading to Mitch shaking his head and walking away in disappointment. Breakout Character: Clem and Mitch would go on to get their very own live-action bumpers onCartoon Network, and also made it intoThe Powerpuff Girls. Butt-Monkey: Clem almost always gets bonked on the head by Mitch. Full-Name Basis: Both of them always refer to each other with the term "Puppet Pal" preceding their names.

characters.name: Action Hank
characters.description: Boisterous Bruiser: His strength is matched only by his good nature and noble intentions. Expy: OfG.I. Joe,Mr. T, andShaft. Foil: "Decode of Honor" establishes him as one to Pony Puff Princess, to spite hisand overly macho exteriorhe's a calm and understanding guy who laughs of Dexter showing up to his club in a tutu with a plate of gingerbread men and rushes to protect Dee Dee when she's in danger. While Pony Puff in spite of hersugary exterioris a violent misandrist who's willing tokill Dee Deejust forshowing up in an army uniformwithout even letting her explain why she did so. Manly Facial Hair: A symbol to his ruggedness, and while he often settles things with his fists, in the episode in which he is introduced, he and Dexter (who had obtained his own beard throughSCIENCE)join beards to fight criminals. Nice Guy: Is actually a friendly individual when not fighting villains despite his intimidating disposition. This is best seen in "Decode of Honor", where his reaction to Dexter showing up in a tutu is to explain that he got his code mixed-up and that Dexter would be in no trouble for this, and when he realizes the code mix-up means that someone else is in trouble, he immediately heads to help.

characters.name: Douglas E. Mordecai III
characters.description: First-Name Basis: The earlier seasons had Dexter refer to him as Douglas but after the show was brought back from cancellation Dexter started calling himMordecaias if healways had been doing so. Ink-Suit Actor: He's basicallyTom Kennyif he were a kid Dexter's age. Nerd Glasses: Like Dexter, he has thick framed glasses that double asEye Glasses. Satellite Character: He's Dexter's best friend. That's pretty much it. This also tends to limit his appearances since many plots revolve around the concept of Dexter having no friends at all.

characters.name: Becky and Gwen
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: Both of them, especially Gwen, who seems to be the more bitchier of the two. The Bully: Both are quite cruel, especially to Dexter. Laser-Guided Karma: They get their comeuppance for causing Dexter to lose his pencil when Billy Bloomberg sticks their heads to the bus ceiling with chewing gum. Pet the Dog: It's implied that Becky is the nicer of the two. She was the first to compliment Dexter's glasses after they got cracked. Took a Level in Kindness: InFramed, they don't really act as mean to Dexter as they did inBus Boy, seeing that they don't make fun of him when his glasses break.

characters.name: Mandark's Parents (Windbear and Oceanbird)
characters.description: Abusive Parents: While they're not the worst examples of the trope, they aren't very supportive of Mandark's love for science, and they gave him a nameSusanthat would subject him to a lot of ridicule from other kids. They also made him dress and act like a girl when he had no interest in doing so. Mandark's father also is the first to actively attempt to shut down Mandark's scientific pursuits and displays anger problems when things don't go his way. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Not only are they hippies, but they had the audacity to name their sonSusan, which eventually helped to push him into his evil tendencies. Berserk Button: Windbear gets mad exactly once, in "My Dad vs. Your Dad", when Dexter's dad makes fun of his hippie lifestyle. Bourgeois Bohemian: Downplayed. They're both pretty conventional for hippies, living in the suburbs with their nuclear family. However, they are completely hippie-esque otherwise, and only left their commune for Mandark's sake. Early-Bird Cameo: Oceanbird's brief, non-speaking appearance in "A Mandark Cartoon" is this due toairing before"A Boy Named Sue", which properly introduced both parents.

characters.name: Pony Puff Princess
characters.description: Does Not Like Men: More specifically, shedespisesanything masculine. As Dee Dee finds out, even women doing or wearing anything masculine won't be spared. My Little Phony: She's the titular character of the in-universe equivalent toyline toMy Little Pony. Nothing Nice About Sugar and Spice: Despite her stereotipically cute appearance and being a hit among young girls, the Pony Puff Princess is actually quite merciless, threatening to eat Dexter, Lee Lee and Mee Mee if they didn't let Dee Dee roam free ("Dee Dee's Tail"), and trying to drip Dee Dee into a cauldron full of boiling oatmeal because she incorrectly wore army-themed clothes and warpaint and got a tattoo, as well as trying to take down Action Hank and his men because they are not feminine ("Decode of Honor"). Royals Who Actually Do Something: She's a Princess and she's willing to fight alongside her fellow Pony Puffs against Action Hank and his men.

characters.name: Lisa the Babysitter
characters.description: Buxom Beauty Standard: She has a pretty well endowed bust, especially for a teenager. Hartman Hips: Due to the art style, lots of women in the series have Hartman Hips. Leg Focus: She wears a plaid skirt that shows off her long, sturdy legs. Ms. Fanservice: She has a slender but curvy figure. Nice Girl: Lisa is shown to be very kind and friendly, and is evidently very good with children, seeing as she's a part-time babysitter.

characters.name: Gary
characters.description: Gary is a bully at Dexter's school. Berserk Button: Children with "funny accents". The Bully: Towards kids with "funny accents". Defeat Means Friendship: After being beaten by the kids with "funny accents", he becomes friends with them. Heel–Face Turn: At the end of the episode.

characters.name: Professor Williams
characters.description: Ink-Suit Actor: He looks a lot like Paul Williams. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is based on (and voiced) by soft rock singerPaul Williams. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Just an Old Fashioned Lab Song".

characters.name: Yani the Janitor
characters.description: Almighty Janitor: A literal case. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Yani is treated as stupid. He made Dexter pay for that remark."It's always the janitor who is stupid, huh Dexter?" Didn't Think This Through:The final phase of his revenge involves him littering the cafeteria floor with potato chips and throwing ketchup packets and forks at Dexter. Apparently it didn't dawn on Yani that by doing so would cause an even bigger mess than what Dexter could make, and thus resulting in more work for Yani. He also forgot the fact that he would still be coming home late and his wife would be pissed.When you also think about it, Yani's also committed multiple crimes - including kidnapping and aggressive battery - in his attempt to get revenge on a student at the school he works at. If, or more accurately, when the school and the authorities would find out about this, he'd lose his job and likely even get arrested. Then, his wife would be even more angry than before. The final phase of his revenge involves him littering the cafeteria floor with potato chips and throwing ketchup packets and forks at Dexter. Apparently it didn't dawn on Yani that by doing so would cause an even bigger mess than what Dexter could make, and thus resulting in more work for Yani. He also forgot the fact that he would still be coming home late and his wife would be pissed. When you also think about it, Yani's also committed multiple crimes - including kidnapping and aggressive battery - in his attempt to get revenge on a student at the school he works at. If, or more accurately, when the school and the authorities would find out about this, he'd lose his job and likely even get arrested. Then, his wife would be even more angry than before.

characters.name: Darbie High Priestess
characters.description: Evil Old Folks: She seems to be an elderly woman and she's a nasty piece of work to boot. Expy: She's meant to be a parody of the Vulcan Minister T'Pau from theStar Trek: The Original Seriesepisode"Amok Time". Oh, Crap!: When she sees that Dexter is about to chuck the turpol at her Darbie doll. One-Shot Character: She along with her fellow Darbie collectors only appear in the episode "Star Check Unconventional" where they were the main antagonists. Serious Business: Removed a Darbie doll from it's box? That's grounds for a serious beating in her eyes.

characters.name: Large Dealer
characters.description: Brawn Hilda: She's a huge lady. Dark Action Girl: She takes on Dexter in a fight after his friend commits theatrociouscrimeof removing a Darbie doll from it's box. The Dragon: To the Darbie High Priestess. Expy: She's meant to be a parody of the Klingons fromStar Trek: The Original Series. Jerkass Has a Point: She isn't wrong to be angry that Dexter's friends ripped open one of her dolls without even paying for it, but trying to kill Dexter over ruining the collector's value isdefinitelyan overreaction.

characters.name: The Dodgeball Bullies
characters.description: Big, Thin, Short Trio: They don't even have names, but one is aFat Bastard, one is tall and skinny, and one is much shorter than the other two. Depraved Dwarf: The Short One. Dirty Coward: They spend most of the climax running away from Dexter's exoskeleton in terror. Although, it can be seen as a case ofKnow When to Fold 'Emgiven that they were facing someone armed with a weapon and they didn't have a weapon of their to fight back against it. Dodgeball Is Hell: They makeithell for Dexter. He then returns the favor by making it hell forthem. Fat Bastard: The Fat One.

characters.name: Olga "Lalavava" Astronomonov
characters.description: Annoying Younger Sibling: Bullies her older brother, Mandark, and bosses him around. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She disappears after her only appearance as later seasons depict Mandark as an only child. Creepy Child: She is aTiny Tyrannical Girlwho likes dark and depressing scary things. Dramatic Thunder: Thunder strikes whenever someone says her name "Lalavava". Enfant Terrible: EvenMandarkis afraid of her.

characters.name: Ice Cream Man
characters.description: Break the Cutie: He had originally enjoyed his job until Dexter paid him in pennies and practically ruined his life. Butt-Monkey: Ever since Dexter bought ice cream from him, and paid him in pennies, a series of unfortunate events had happened to him since, including chipping his tooth while trying to put them in the safe due to tripping on his laces after counting them, dumped by his girlfriend, having his car towed away, getting kicked out of his apartment and being forced to live under a highway because of this one act.And to add insult to injury, once the Ice Cream Man forgives Dexter and allows him to purchase ice cream, Dexter pays the Ice Cream Man with a 100 dollar bill. And to add insult to injury, once the Ice Cream Man forgives Dexter and allows him to purchase ice cream, Dexter pays the Ice Cream Man with a 100 dollar bill. Jerkass Has a Point: While no one would argue (especially people who work in similar industries) against the fact that not serving Dexter was rude, Dexter had paid for an expensive ice cream with pennies (which took him 5 hours to count),causing him to trip over his own shoelaces, chip his teeth, return home too late to pay the rent (which got him kicked out of his apartment), getting his car impounded, having his girlfriend dump him and ending up having to live with wild animals under the freeway.

characters.name: Computress
characters.description: A sentient computer created by Mandark. He only appears in "Dexter and Computress Get Mandark!". Butt-Monkey: Bad things seem to happen to him whether he works for Mandark or Dexter. When he worked for Mandark, Mandark would destroy his laboratory and make Computress rebuild it by himself, and when he worked for Dexter, he accidentally enlarged Mandark's head instead of shrinking it and got chewed out by Dexter as a result. Gender-Blender Name: Computress is a male computer, but has a feminine name. Robo Family: Computress is introduced as Mandark's brother,apparently. Turned Against Their Masters: Computress turned against Mandark and teamed up with Dexter to shrink Mandark's head because Mandark destroyed his laboratory and made Computress rebuild it by himself.

characters.name: The Neighborhood Criminal
characters.description: Caring Gardener: He turns outnot to be a criminal as Dee-Dee, Lee-Lee and Mee-Mee thought, but rather a friendly and harmless gardener. Not Helping Your Case: Even thoughhe turned out not to be a criminal, he didn't make Dee-Dee and her two friends any less suspicious of him by cutting a branch off of the tree that the three girls' treehouse was in.

characters.name: Mc Bark The Crime Dog
characters.description: Dull Surprise: He (The man playing him in the episode at least) speaks in a bored and disinterested tone. Expy: He is clearly a parody ofMcGruffThe Crime Dog. Hidden Depths: Despite acting initially like the stereotypical bored minimum wage mascot worker who only goes through the motions of his job, he shows up at the end of the episode, unprompted, to give the"Lesson of the Day" Speechand deliver his mascot's catchphrase "This crime's been licked!" evengrinningslightly as he does it. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His dull manner of speaking makes one wonder if the producers originally wanted to getBen Steinto voice him.

characters.name: The Detention Warden
characters.description: Big "NO!": He screams one when Dexter and the other "criminals" escape at the end of the episode. Catchphrase: Uses the word "criminal" a lot. With a close-up on his mouth for emphasis. Evil Laugh: He laughs sadistically during the sequence where Dexter and the other "criminals"write "I am a criminal" on the chalkboard. Jerkass: He refuses to listen to Dexter's protests of innocence and treats the students as low-life criminals. Monster of the Week: Only appears inDexter Detentionwhere he was the main antagonist.

characters.name: Sassy
characters.description: Big-Hearted Bigfoot: He turns out to rather kind and all happy to play with Dee-Dee. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: As a sasquatch he's this to the much smaller Dee Dee. Interspecies Friendship: His best friend is Dee Dee, a human girl.

characters.name: Gork
characters.description: AnETwho thought Dexter looked delicious. Big Eater: He is shown to be perpetually hungry as seen when he ate all the food in the space prison cafeteria and then tries to eat Dexter when he saw there was no more food in the prison. Cruel Elephant: Has an elephant-like shape and was intending to eat Dexter when there was no food left for him. I'm a Humanitarian: He was going to eat Dexter when he learned that there was nothing left in the prison cafeteria. Graceful Loser: When Dee-Dee offers him a turkey dinner as an alternative to eating Dexter, he just decides to eat that instead.

characters.name: Dextor's Parents
characters.description: Identical Stranger: To Dexter's Parents. They're both smart yet cold and unfeeling while Dexter's Parents, despite their faults, are still loving. Obliviously Evil: While they're certainly cold and unfeeling, they probably genuinely don't understand other's emotions.

characters.name: The King and Queen of Koosland
characters.description: Nice Guy: They're both kind and fair rulers. It's best seen when The King stops the rest of the Koosland residents from attempting to kill Koosie and forgives Koosie for the whole fiasco. Santa Claus: The King seems to be Koosland's equivalent what with his role of travelling around the world giving toys to the good girls and boys.

characters.name: Hookocho
characters.description: Agent Peacock: While he is a threateningAlien Prince, he also looks like a very pretty woman. AFreeze-Frame Bonusalso reveals thathis nails◊are painted. Alien Prince: Or at least imaginary alien. Animesque: He is a parody ofBishōnenanime characters with his effeminate appearance and heels. Conquering Alien Prince: He's a parody of this trope, as manyMecha AnimeofThe '70sandThe '80shad them as villains (such asGigantor,Voltes VandDaimos). The Dog Bites Back: Hookocho spends most of the episode abusing Peepers and telling him no will one come save him. He is defeated when Peepers grows in size and stomps on him.

characters.name: Soyen Chen
characters.description: A transfer student who's a genius like Dexter and Mandark, much to their shared dismay and jealousy. Abhorrent Admirer: After Dexter and Mandark admit defeat to her, she tells them that she's no longer interested in science... but now interested in boys. CueOh, Crap!looks on their faces andthem running awaywhile she chases them and blowing kisses. Always Someone Better: To Dexter and Mandark after she won first place at a science fair until she loses interest in science. Asian and Nerdy: She's Asian and wears glasses while being potentially smarter than Dexter and Mandark. Unknown Rival: She isn't aware that Dexter and Mandark are trying to destroy her because she's smarter than them until she sees them having a slapfight in theirHumongous Mechawhen they originally intended to attack her with them, prompting her todisable them by using her home's sprinklers which forces them to eject.

characters.name: Badaxtra
characters.description: Go Out with a Smile: Badaxtra has an unimpressed smirk on its face as the Dexter robot is coming at it with a super punch. The punch makes Badaxtraexplode. Hero Killer: It defeats Global Security, The Justice Friends and Monkey by itself. Knight of Cerebus: Dexter had to reveal his laboratory to his parents to count on them and be able to defeat him. Sealed Evil in a Can: Badaxtra was kept prisoner in a volcano back in the 1960's until Dexter accidentally fired missiles at it. Weapon Specialization: It's face, tail, claws and even toes are axe-shaped.

characters.name: Parallax and Red-Eye
characters.description: Bad Boss: Red-Eye is harsh boss and his lackeys all fear him. The Dog Was the Mastermind: High Commander Mat Parallax runs a lonely photo booth at the mall. In truth, he is the leader of an evil organization. Dragon-in-Chief: Red-Eye runs the day-to-day operations at the photo lab. Expy: Red-Eye looks like the stereotypical James Bond villain but his master-apprentice relationship with Parallax is an unsubtle reference to Darth Vader and The Emperor. Hoist by His Own Petard: Red-Eye is zapped by his own camera/death ray.

characters.name: The Paper Ninjas
characters.description: Bad People Abuse Animals: When they first appear, they throw a newspaper at one of the neighbors'catas well as a bird nest. Later on, during the paper route race, the ninja Dee-Dee is competing against throws a newspaper at some birds and then nearly hits a squirrel, prompting the squirrel to retaliate by chucking a acorn at him. Delinquents: They smash windows as well as coffee mugs. Jerkass: Where do we start? first they chuck newspapers at the neighbors causing them to spill their coffee over themselves as well as chucking one at one of the neighbors'catand the house's windows and the neighbors' coffee mugs then when Dee-Dee confronts them for what they did, they chuck newspapers ather.The Ninja that Dee-Dee competes against purposefully throws a paper at a flock of birds and a squirrel as well as attacking a man carrying china and small animals when he was meant to be throwing them at the houses. Monster of the Week: They only appear inPaper Route Bout. More Hateable Minor Villain: Not even Mandark stooped as low as committing vandalism even inthe moviecompared to these guys.

characters.name: Earl
characters.description: The Faceless: He's only shown from the neck down. Jerkass: He makes his arm wrestling matches painful for his opponents, has a go with Dad for accidentally making him lose one of them, trashes Dad's car and then slams the door on Mom when she tries to get her purse. Laser-Guided Karma: When he gets chucked out of the cafe. Monster of the Week: He only appears inHamhocks And Armlockswhere he was the main antagonist. Sore Loser: He challenges Dad to arm-wrestling for unintentionally causing his first ever loss by changing the jukebox music, allowing the challenger to win from the distraction.

characters.name: Master Computer
characters.description: A.I. Is a Crapshoot: He is a sentient computer program who intends to take over Dexter's lab, and quite possibly the world. Expy: He is based on theMCPfromTron Would Hurt a Child: After transporting Dexter into his domain, Master Computer had no qualms about pitting him against several obstacles like falling Tetris blocks, and a giant Pac-Man like monster.

characters.name: Monkey
characters.description: Dexter's pet monkey and Earth's greatest superhero. The Ace:In-Universe, he is the most powerful and respected hero on the planet. Aliens however tend to underestimate him due to his appearance, which always ends poorly for them. Also, he has a beautiful girlfriend. Action Pet: When off-duty, his personality is similar to Dee Dee's and he is often seenplaying with her in the laboratory, but when it is time to save the world Monkey is extremely serious and heroic and risks his very life to ensure the safety of the world and those he loves. Almighty Janitor: As far as Dexter is concerned, Monkey will never be anything more than a normal, average monkey. Amplified Animal Aptitude: Even without his powers, Monkey is just as intelligent — if not moreso — than all the humans around him.

characters.name: Agent Honeydew
characters.description: Action Girl: As part of her agent training, she is a trained fighter who is proficient in firearms. Boyish Short Hair: She has short black hair with curly bangs. Fights Like a Normal: Honeydew possesses telepathic powers but primarily uses them to communicate with Monkey. In battle, she relies on her hand-to-hand combat training and use of firearms. Expy: Of Agent 13 ofThe Avengers Interspecies Romance: Despite their different species' (and the questionable ethics of this), it appears that Monkey and Honeydew's relationship is very close and romantic, as both are often seen going out on dates when off-duty, sharing romantic dinners, and Monkey sometimes stays over at her house, where they apparently bathe together while she grooms him.

characters.name: Commander Chief
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: While he definitely looks human, he only ever appears on TV screens and is never seen in person. In "Huntor", his TV set was tied up and suspended over lava by the titular villain, and the episode treated him as though he was in legitimate danger, implying that he was actually an image projected on the screen. While it's possible that it wasjust a throwaway gag for the sake of the episode, another episode, "Organ Grindor", has him attempt to get a sample of Agent Honeydew's cooking, but can't because, as she herself said, he's trapped in "that box". Big Good: By way of being the head of the organization Agent Honeydew works for, he's the highest authority figure Monkey works for. Expy: OfNick Fury, both characters being leaders of police organizations who wear eyepatches. Eyepatch of Power: To go with the mustache, he also wears an eyepatch. Punny Name: Commander(-in) Chief.

characters.name: The Silver Spooner
characters.description: Barbecuor's culinary guide, herald and personal valet. Attention Deficit... Oh, Shiny!: He is distracted when he thought thatJudy Garlandwas around. Camp Straight: He has very camp gestures and sensibilities. Expy: His resemblance to Marvel's Silver Surfer led to the "Barbecuor" episode getting banned in America. Hoist by His Own Petard: Monkey batters him over the head with his own Silver Spoon. Monkey then uses the spoon to extract Earth from Barbequor's throat.

characters.name: Barbequor
characters.description: Curb-Stomp Battle: He makes short work of Earth's defenders. Though Monkey stops him from devouring Earth, he is never defeated either. Does This Remind You of Anything?: His way of eating planet is to barbecue them. And he literally treats the planet's heroes as mere insects. Expy: He's a parody ofGalactus. Galactic Conqueror: The Eater of Worlds travels the galaxy for planets to eat. Planet Eater: He takes the planets of the solar system and tries to eat them like a shish kebab.

characters.name: Magmanamus
characters.description: Anti-Villain: He doesn't really want to hurt anyone. All he wanted was to get some sleep. Ceiling Banger: A massive version of this. "Could Have Avoided This!" Plot: It doesn't occur to Magmanamus that he could just move somewhere quieter (to another planet, specifically). Eldritch Abomination: Parodied. His "Ancient Evilinvincible monster frombeneath the earthawakened by human arrogance" schtick is a classic plotline, but his nature, motives and personality are hilariously human. Gaia's Vengeance: Also parodied. He's taking revenge fornoisepollution.

characters.name: Rasslor
characters.description: Some wrestlingETdude. Affably Evil: A world destroying alien wrestler who will show respect to his worthy adversaries and even honorable attempts like Major Glory."Major Glory, you speak boldly and your breath is minty fresh. For this, I salute you." Barbarian Long Hair: Reaches to the small of his back. Boisterous Bruiser: A given being voiced by Macho Man Randy Savage. Blood Knight: Loves to wrestle and fight.

characters.name: Promotor
characters.description: Expy: A parody of controversial boxing promoter Don King, who may be best known for having acted as Mike Tyson's manager. Kneel Before Zod: He commands the Justice Friends to bow to Rasslor. One-Shot Character: Appears in the episode "Rasslor"

characters.name: Quackor the Fowl/Ducky
characters.description: A Dog Named "Dog": Her real name is Ducky. Dark Action Girl: After she's revealed to be female in her second appearance, we learn that she's this. Evil Counterpart: To Monkey. She is Mandark's pet duck and Monkey's arch-nemesis. Feathered Fiend: An evil duck. Gender Flip: Originally presented as a male character in their first appearance, later retconned into a female for their second (and last) appearance.

characters.name: Simion
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's a very sophisticated villain who even has abanquetprepared for Monkey when he breaks into his base before telling him he plans to vaporize the Earth in five minutes. Apes in Space: Before being mutated by gamma rays, Simion was an ordinary chimpanzee launched into space as a test subject. Dark and Troubled Past: Originally a normal chimp astronaut before a crack in his spacecraft caused it to explode, flinging him deep into space and exposed him to gamma radiation. This granted him super-intelligence and powerful kinetic abilities, but it forced him to spend the next 50 years in isolation preparing his revenge on humanity. The Dog Bites Back: He wants revenge on humanity as he deemed them responsible for his ship's explosion and the resulting accident that made him who he is now. Evil Counterpart: To Monkey. Both gained superpowers as a result of human experimentation. Monkey became a superhero while Simion turned to villainy due to the bitterness over being abandoned by humans.

characters.name: Orgon Grindor
characters.description: And I Must Scream: Ends up encased in gold while still conscious. Fat Bastard: Overweight and a nasty crook. Funny Foreigner: He speaks in a stereotypical Italian accent. Greed: He tries to hypnotize Monkey into stealing valuables for him. Musical Assassin: HisMind-Control Deviceis a music player used to entrance Monkey. Not only that, but he sings nearly every time he's on screen.

characters.name: Peltra
characters.description: Bald of Evil: She has no hair whatsoever. Honeydew lampshades theIronyof a hairless villain stealing other animals' fur to wear herself. Barbie Doll Anatomy: When stripped naked by Agent Honeydew, her exposed body is devoid of genitalia or any other detail. Cruella to Animals: She hires her goons Tanner and Skinner to kill animals just so she can have them made into exotic clothes. Cat Fight: With Honeydew, complete with hissing and noises. She's even wearing an outfit made of cat's hide at the time. Designated Girl Fight: Honeydew takes her down; Monkey takes out her minions and wraps her up afterwards.

characters.name: Huntor
characters.description: Aliens of London: Huntor is an alien who speaks with an Australian accent. Badass Normal: Huntor doesn't have any superpowers and relies on his weaponry and skills as a hunter. Beast of Battle: Uses his biomechanicalSnorkdroas a steed to pursue his prey, at least until it's incapacitated. BFG: Whips out a tricked-out rifle nearly twice as long as he is tall in his attempt to take down Monkey. Unfortunately for him, that made it easier to destroy. The Cameo: In an episode ofSamurai Jack.

characters.name: As a Whole
characters.description: Adaptational Personality Change: The Justice Friends appear in "Dexter's Laboratory" as comical but sincerely well-meaning heroes, but are seen to be misogynistic males in the "Powerpuff Girls show" show. Awesome, but Impractical: The comedy comes from the heroes trying ordinary occurrences with superhero panache/powers, when common sense and reason would have worke better. The title sequence for the skits involve the Justice Friends fumbling atchanging a lightbulb. Composite Character: The group's name is a portmanteau of theJustice Leagueand theSuperfriendsfromDC Comics, but the cast is largely derived fromMarvel Comicssuperheroes, particularlyThe Avengers. Cast of Expies: All of them are copies or parodies of other superheroes.Major Glory:Captain America(withSuperman'spowers)Valhallen:The Mighty Thorwith a transformation scheme based onHe-Man.The Infraggable Krunk:The Incredible HulkLiving Bullet:Iron Manvisually, but withQuicksilver'sandFlash'spowersWhite Tiger:Black PantherMiss Spell:Scarlet WitchCapital G:Black GoliathTiki Torch:Human TorchSnow Man:Ice ManPhan Tone:Visionwith DC'sDeadmanSam-R-I:Silver SamuraiRatman:BatmanThere are two unnamed heroes as well. One resembles Beast from The X-Men, except he's yellow instead of blue. The other resembles Hawkeye from The Avengers except he's green like The Green Arrow. Major Glory:Captain America(withSuperman'spowers)

characters.name: Major Glory
characters.description: Adaptational Personality Change: When he appears in theThe Powerpuff Girls (1998)episode "Members Only", he displays sexist and ageist attitudes towards the girls, not taking them seriously because they're girls and young girls at that. This contrasts with his appearance in the episode "Star-Spangled Sidekicks" where he was willing to work with teenage superheroes and found Dee Dee the most impressive out of all the kids who auditioned to be his sidekick. Due to multiple inconsistencies between the two shows however, this is likely a different Major Glory to begin with (nothing is known of him outside of his identity). Afraid of Doctors: Or more specifically, implied to be afraid of dentists. Ambiguously Human: His uncle is Uncle Sam, who is theAnthropomorphic Personificationof the United States and the series' wiki states Major Glory is human,buthe has the powers ofFlightand eye-beams, making it unclear as to whether he's human or aDifferently Powered Individualor even aHalf-Human Hybrid. He looks and acts human enough, making it unclear as to what he really is. Then again, he is aSuperman Substitute, so hemaynot be human anyway. As it stands, official canon does not state whether he is human or not. The Cape: Played for laughs - he tries to live up to his heroic principles, but tends toward obliviousness and narrow-mindedness. Captain Patriotic: He even hawks a snack named "Justice Fruit Pies", and periodically recites lyrics or lines from famous American works (such as the national anthem, the Constitution, and the Pledge of Allegiance).

characters.name: Valhallen
characters.description: Barbarian Longhair: Very long blond hair. Bigger on the Inside: His room. There's an episode dedicated to it, appropriately titled "Valhallen's Room". Chick Magnet: Being a parody of rock stars, it's no surprise that he's very popular with the fairer sex. He has a bunch of wildly screaming female fans when he steps into the ring in "Wrasslor". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Disappeared after the show wasUn-Cancelled, along with the other Justice Friends. Though they did get an appearance in "Dexter's Wacky Races". Cowardly Lion: Like Major Glory, he's absolutely terrified of bees.

characters.name: The Infraggable Krunk
characters.description: Adapted Out: Krunk was strangely excluded from the version of the team that appears inThe Powerpuff Girls (1998). This is even pointed out within the show; Bubbles asks her sisters if Krunk would appear, with Buttercup replying he was "too stupid to join." Adult Sleeps with Stuffed Toy: To emphasize hisManchildstatus, he is shown sleeping with a stuffed toy. Ambiguously Human: Since he looks like a purple-skinned humanoid and (unlike his inspiration) doesn't appear to have a non-powered form to revert to, it's not clear if he's a human or just a member of a human-like species. Berserk Button: As Major Glory and Valhallen learn the hard way, don't destroy the TV while he's watching "Puppet Pals". The Big Guy: The muscle-man of the Justice Friends.

characters.name: White Tiger
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: His repeated back-and-forth swings between human-like intelligence (being a super hero, engaging in conversations with Valhallen and bipedal locomotion) and cat-like behaviours (wanting to play with a loose string, licking milk, sleeping like a cat, and only growling and purring) makes it unclear whether he's anAnimal-Themed Superbeing, aBeast Man, or either a case ofAmplified Animal Aptitudeor anUplifted Animal. Anvil on Head: Drops an anvil on Krunk's head when he's disguised as a mouse as aShout-OuttoTom and Jerry. Big Damn Heroes: White Tiger makes his first appearance rescuing Valhallen from the supervillain Mental Mouse. The Blank: White Tiger's mask hides all but his yellow eyes. Expy: Most likely of Marvel'sBlack Panther, being anAnimal-Themed SuperbeingColor Character.noteWhat’s hilarious however is that Marvel comics indeed hasa character called White Tiger,who had debuted in 1975, 21 years earlier.

characters.name: Tiki Torch
characters.description: Mundane Utility: He uses his fire powers to make flaming punch drink for Monkey's birthday.

characters.name: Miss Spell
characters.description: Captain Ersatz: Being a spell-casting superheroine in a red, she seems to be based onScarlet Witch. Oh, Crap!: She says "Oh, hex" after seeing how huge Barbecuor is. The Smurfette Principle: She is the only female member of the Justice Friends.

characters.name: Capital G
characters.description: Always Someone Better: He grows to full size in "Last But Not Beast", but he is still smaller than the monster, who casually andliterallyflicks him away. Black Dude Dies First: He is the first Justice League member to be beaten by Badaxtra. Expy: Is likely based on Marvel's Black Goliath, being an African American with size-changing powers. Sizeshifter: He usually uses his power to become gigantic, but at one point shrunk to try and extract Krunk's aching tooth. Ultraman Copy:Downplayed. As a size-changing black hero who is a member of the Justice Friends, he more closely resembles Marvel Comics character Bill Foster/Black Goliath. However, his red/blue/white color scheme and goggles, coupled with him turning giant during the episode "Last But Not Beast" to fight the giant monster Badaxtra during the latter's rampage in Japan, give him a faint resemblance to Ultraman.

characters.name: Living Bullet
characters.description: Captain Ersatz: Of Bulletman. Super-Speed: He also talks fast.

characters.name: Snow Man
characters.description: A Dog Named "Dog": A snowman who became a superhero named Snow Man. The Load: He is the only Justice Friend member who refuses to fight Barbequor. He's just there to party.

characters.name: Ratman
characters.description: Adaptation-Induced Plot Hole: One that is invoked and commented on in-universe. He is a blatant spoof of Batman, but with his parents beingSpared by the Adaptation, instead simply being scared off by rats. After Ratman explains how the same rats took him in and cared for him, the Justice Friends are more confused than ever about him. Valhallen notes his story doesn't make sense because the rats are the ones who scared his parents away in the first place, and he doesn't really have any motivation for being a hero and "avenging his parents" since they aren't dead or anything. Art Evolution: He has a cameo among the members of A.W.S.M. inThe Powerpuff Girls (1998)episode "Members Only", where he's redesigned to look more like Batman, but with whiskers and differently-positioned pointy ears. Batman Parody: With the name just having the first letter changed to an R, he is a blatantBatmanspoof. His origin even involves losing his parents after leaving a movie theater (including his mother's beaded necklace falling apart), albeit not in a way that gets them killed. Comically Missing the Point: He seems to think that his "tragic backstory" and costume is all it takes to be a crime-fighter, and when the Justice Friends are confused by his story, with Valhallen pointing out a few plot-holes that don't make sense and questioning his motivation for wanting to be a hero, he is just confused as to how they aren't getting that he's supposed to be a superhero.Valhallen:Wait dude, your story don't add up. I mean, aren't the rats the ones who scared your parents away? Then... what, Ratman, what's the motivation here? Are you like, avenging your parents, or...?Ratman:What do you mean? I got the costume, the belt. What's not to get? Hidden Depths: He might be a fatManchildand have a confusing origin story, but he actually does have some talents with machines. When the Justice Friends try to stop a boiler from blowing with brute force and completely fail, he simply tells them to stop pl

characters.name: Comrade Red
characters.description: Dirty Communists: He's a stereotypical Communist Russian and a supervillain. Expy: He is most likely based on Marvel Comics villain the Red Skull, since he's a supervillain with "Red" in his name and is the main foe of Major Glory, himself a parody of the Red Skull's nemesis Captain America; notably, the Red Skull identity was appropriated by a communist named Albert Malik at one point. The Russian theme may also be a nod to DC character Red Star. Evil Counterpart: He serves as a villainous version of Major Glory. Hammer and Sickle: Both present in his costume and wielding them as weapons, as seen in his image. Heel–Face Turn: Appears among Major Glory and the otherDexter's Laboratoryheroes as a member of hero team A.W.S.M. inThe Powerpuff Girls (1998)episode "Members Only".

characters.name: She-Thing
characters.description: Dating Catwoman: In spite of being on opposite sides in the war against good and evil, she and Krunk fall in love with each other. Distaff Counterpart: She is essentially a female version of Krunk. Evil Counterpart: For all intents and purposes, she's an evil equivalent to Krunk. HULK MASH!-Up: She's whatShe-Hulkwould be like if she were evil, dumb, and not related to the Hulk.

characters.name: Minotaur
characters.description: An evil record producer and music manager who enslaves singers. He captured the Sirens and forced them to sing to create his new hit album (which when distributed, will make him rule the world) but promptly lets them go once Valhallen got involved. Friendly Enemy: Minotaur is apparently a superhero fanboy who allows his plans to be thwarted if he could get an autograph from them. Afterward, he remains affable and chummy. Our Minotaurs Are Different: Minotaur is portrayed as a humanoid bull. The Knights Who Say "Squee!": Minotaur is a big fan of Valhallen and immediately released the Sirens and halted his evil plans just so he could get the latter's autograph. Take Over the World: Minotaur plans to use the Sirens' song to conquer the globe (with the proper distribution and cross-promotion).

characters.name: Disgruntled Postman
characters.description: A villain with a postal service gimmick. Ax-Crazy: He attempted to mail abombto the President of the United States. Death Dealer: He hurls razor sharp bills that cut Major Glory's cheek. Didn't Think This Through: His mail bomb looks like it should be dropped from a plane. He also fights Major Glory, aFlying Brick, by throwing bills at him. Expy: He's a rather obviousJokerparody because he's an insane criminal who has chalk-white skin, green hair, red lips, and a manic grin; literally the Joker dressed as a mailman.
